sources.purpose: Exact Grove Questionnaire proposal base retained for review and same-repository proposal composition.
Exact Grove Mobile and HealthKit proposal base used to materialize the current Swift contract.
Historical Grove 0.2.1 baseline retained for later deterministic semantic compatibility evidence.
Inactive Grove SensorKit proposal tip retained for provenance and reference only; no proposal is materialized from it.
Exact My Heart Counts iOS application revision retained for cross-platform conformance evidence.
Exact My Heart Counts Android base used to materialize the Health Connect proposal.
Exact My Heart Counts Firebase base used to materialize the source-neutral FHIR receiver proposal.
Exact StudyDefinitions 0.2.4 dependency pinned by the retained My Heart Counts iOS revision.
Exact StudyDefinitions 0.2.5 revision retained as the later study-revision evidence baseline.

claims: Grove Swift imports and exports the reviewed versioned Questionnaire contract and imports and exports QuestionnaireResponse resources without silently dropping supported semantic content.

Completed and amended responses fail closed when enablement, requiredness, target constraints, answer nesting, types, repeats, or versioned choice membership cannot be evaluated or do not match the referenced Questionnaire.
Deterministic Questionnaire and QuestionnaireResponse fixtures round-trip through the public implementation and pass both the repository pair checker and the exact R4 Questionnaire package.
The default Grove Swift HealthKit adapter emits only heart rate, body weight, and exact-interval step count under the reviewed Mobile and HealthKit profiles, and fails closed for other source types.

HealthKit source identity is a complete lowercase UUID business identifier, while recording device, actual gateway, explicitly classified source author, and converter assembler remain distinct provenance roles; ambiguous source authors are omitted.

Recording method and ResearchStudy attribution are emitted only from explicit evidence, using the Grove recording-method extension and the standard workflow-researchStudy extension without retired canonicals or metadata shortcuts.

The Android Health Connect adapter emits complete FHIR R4 collection Bundles for exactly StepsRecord, WeightRecord, and HeartRateRecord under the reviewed Grove Mobile, Health Connect, and applicable domain profiles, and fails closed for every other record type.

Repository-scoped pseudonymous source identities, deterministic one-to-many output identities, distinct source-application/converter/recorder roles, and immutable conversion Provenance and companion resources preserve the reviewed identity and provenance contract without exposing the raw Health Connect id or hidden repository scope.

A projection-scoped token lease, durable boundary-baseline-drain recovery, enumerable exact-byte outbox, authoritative event sequence, complete update/deletion tombstones, valid zero-output state, and fail-consistent receiver limits prevent token progress from losing or stranding an accepted source projection.

The source-neutral receiver library accepts only complete FHIR R4 collection Bundle JSON under a strict five-field envelope, preserves the exact submitted Bundle bytes and companion resources, and performs structural and complete-identifier checks without exposing an unauthenticated intake endpoint or claiming full profile validation.

A trusted server-derived partition plus complete source and Observation identifiers scope collision-safe indexes, while authoritative per-source event sequences provide exact replay, newer replacement, tombstone-only update, deletion, stale-event rejection, and complete output-set ownership without synthesizing lossy FHIR resources.

Generation-pinned immutable Bundle and manifest objects, paged transactional claims, a leased at-least-once outbox, bounded retry/dead-letter and garbage-collection quarantine, and generation-aware metadata retirement support complete series beyond 200 samples; 16 MiB, 50,000-Observation, and 80,000-token receiver limits reject an entire event without truncation, and the frozen Android vectors are checked at their exact producer byte hashes.
